steps.prompt: You are the red car. You want to pass the blue car. Which lane do you use to pass? Tap the lane.

targets.label: the nearest lane for cars coming toward you

then.say: You pass in the lane on your left. The line between your lane and that lane is a broken white line, and you may cross a broken white line to pass or change lanes when it is safe.

wrong.oncoming-lane: Two solid yellow lines lie between your lane and that lane, and they are never crossed to pass, from either direction. You pass in the lane on your left, across the broken white line.

steps.rule: You may cross a broken white line between lanes to pass or change lanes when it is safe.

steps.prompt: You are the red car. The blue car is slow, and no car is coming toward you. The center of the road has two solid yellow lines. May you cross them to pass the blue car?
options: Yes
No

then.say: No, you stay behind the blue car. Two solid yellow lines may not be crossed to pass from either direction, even when no car is coming toward you. You may cross them to turn into a driveway or a side road when it is safe.

wrong.Yes: No car is coming, but two solid yellow lines may not be crossed to pass from either direction, even then. You stay behind the blue car.

steps.rule: Two solid yellow lines mean you may not cross them to pass from either direction, even when no car is coming toward you.

steps.prompt: You are the red car. The blue car is slow. The center line on your side is a broken yellow line. The road goes over the top of a hill, and you cannot see the shaded part beyond it. May you pass the blue car now?
options: Yes
No

then.say: No, you stay behind the blue car until you can see the road ahead. Beyond the top of the hill a car is coming toward you, where you could not see it. You do not pass when coming up to a hill or a curve, even where the broken yellow line is on your side.

wrong.Yes: The broken yellow line on your side allows passing only when you can see that no car is coming, and the hill hides the road beyond its top. At a hill you do not pass, even where the broken line is on your side. You stay behind the blue car.

steps.rule: You do not pass when you are coming up to a hill or a curve, because you cannot see the cars coming toward you.

steps.prompt: You are the red car. Two solid yellow lines are on your right, and a broken white line is on your left. What do the lines tell you?
options: You are going the wrong way.
You are in a passing zone.
You are in the correct lane.
steps.answer: You are going the wrong way.

then.say: You are going the wrong way. Yellow lines belong on a driver's left, so yellow on your right means this lane is for cars coming toward you. You move out of it as soon as it is safe.

A passing zone has a broken yellow line on your side, and the yellow lines on this road are solid and on your right. Yellow on your right and white on your left means you are going the wrong way.
In the correct lane the yellow lines are on your left. Yellow on your right means this lane is for cars coming toward you, so you are going the wrong way. You move out of it as soon as it is safe.

steps.rule: If you have yellow lines on your right and a white line on your left, you are going the wrong way.

steps.prompt: You are the red car. You want to pass the motorcycle. Which lane do you use to pass? Tap the lane.

targets.label: the lane the motorcycle is in

then.say: You pass in the lane on your left. A motorcycle has the use of its whole lane, even when the rider is near one edge, so you pass it as you would pass a car.

wrong.moto-lane: A motorcycle has the use of its whole lane, so you never share a lane with it, even when the rider is near the edge. You pass in the lane on your left.

steps.rule: A motorcycle has the right to use its whole lane, so you never share a lane with it.

steps.prompt: You are the red car. You want to pass the bicycle. How much space does the law require between your car and the bicycle?
options: The law requires at least 1 foot.
The law requires at least 3 feet.
The law requires at least 6 feet.
steps.answer: The law requires at least 3 feet.

then.say: The law requires at least 3 feet between your car and the bicycle. You keep that space until you are past the bicycle, and you pass slowly.

One foot is less than the law requires. The law requires at least 3 feet, kept until you are past the bicycle.
Six feet is more than the law requires. The law requires at least 3 feet, kept until you are past the bicycle.

steps.rule: When you pass a bicycle going your way, the law requires at least 3 feet between your car and the bicycle until you are past it.

steps.prompt: You are the red car. You want to move into the lane on your left. The blue car is in that lane just behind your door, in the shaded spot that neither of your mirrors shows. How do you check for it before you move over?
options: You turn your head and look over your left shoulder.
You check your inside mirror only.
You check your outside mirror only.
steps.answer: You turn your head and look over your left shoulder.

then.say: You turn your head and look over your left shoulder. Your mirrors leave a blind spot beside and just behind your car, so you look over your shoulder in the direction you will move.

The inside mirror shows the road behind you, not the spot beside you, so the blue car stays hidden. You turn your head and look over your left shoulder.
The outside mirror leaves a blind spot beside and just behind your car, and the blue car is in it. You turn your head and look over your left shoulder.

steps.rule: Before you change lanes, you turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you will move, because your mirrors leave a blind spot.

steps.prompt: You are the red car, passing the blue car on a two-lane road. When do you move back into your lane?
options: You move back when you can see both of the blue car's headlights in your rearview mirror.
You move back as soon as your front bumper is past the blue car's front bumper.
You move back when the blue car's driver waves you over.
steps.answer: You move back when you can see both of the blue car's headlights in your rearview mirror.

then.say: You move back when you can see both of the blue car's headlights in your rearview mirror. Then there is room between your car and the blue car, and you do not count on its driver to make room for you.

wrong.You move back as soon as your front bump: With only your front bumper past, most of your car is still beside the blue car, and moving over would hit it. Even now, just ahead of it, you are too close to its front to move over. You wait until you can see both of its headlights in your rearview mirror.
wrong.You move back when the blue car's driver: You do not count on another driver to make room for you, and a wave does not show you the room between your car and the blue car. You wait until you can see both of its headlights in your rearview mirror.

steps.rule: After you pass a car, you move back into your lane when you can see both of its headlights in your rearview mirror.

steps.prompt: You are the red car. The blue car has its left turn signal on and is slowing to turn left into the driveway. There is room to pass it on its right side without leaving your lane. May you pass the blue car on the right?
options: Yes
No

then.say: Yes, you may pass the blue car on the right when it is safe. On a two-lane road, passing on the right is allowed only when the car ahead is turning left. You never pass on the left of a car that is turning left.

wrong.No: The blue car is turning left, and that is the one time a two-lane road allows passing on the right, when it is safe. You may pass it on the right, staying in your lane.

steps.rule: On a two-lane road, you may pass on the right only when the car ahead is turning left and it is safe.

steps.prompt: You are the red car. The blue car is slow and going straight. A paved shoulder runs along the right edge of the road. May you pass the blue car on the shoulder?
options: Yes
No

then.say: No, you stay behind the blue car. You never drive on the shoulder to pass, even when it is paved. On a two-lane road you pass on the right only when the car ahead is turning left.

wrong.Yes: The shoulder is not a lane, and you never drive on it to pass, even when it is paved. On a two-lane road you pass on the right only when the car ahead is turning left, and the blue car is going straight.

steps.rule: You never pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder.

steps.prompt: You are the red car, 100 feet behind the truck in the same lane. Can the truck driver see your car?
options: Yes
No

then.say: No, the truck driver cannot see your car. The shaded areas are the truck's blind spots: directly in front of it, on both sides, and up to 200 feet behind it. At 100 feet back you are in the one behind it.

wrong.Yes: A truck's blind spot behind it reaches up to 200 feet, so at 100 feet back its driver cannot see your car. Its other blind spots are directly in front of it and on both sides.

steps.rule: A truck's blind spots are directly in front of it, on both sides, and up to 200 feet behind it.

steps.prompt: You are the red car, beside the middle of the truck's trailer, going the same speed as the truck. What do you do?
options: You stay beside the truck, so its driver knows you are there.
You pass the truck when it is safe, so you do not stay beside it.
steps.answer: You pass the truck when it is safe, so you do not stay beside it.

then.say: You pass the truck when it is safe, so you do not stay beside it. Both sides of a truck are blind spots, and beside its trailer its driver cannot see your car.

wrong.You stay beside the truck, so its driver: Beside its trailer you are in one of the truck's blind spots, so its driver cannot see your car. You pass the truck when it is safe, so you do not stay beside it.

steps.rule: Both sides of a truck are blind spots, so you do not stay beside a truck.
